newsitem.title: JAPAN: Loss-hit Sumitomo proposes bonus cuts for staff.
newsitem.headline: Loss-hit Sumitomo proposes bonus cuts for staff.

text.p: Sumitomo Corp, burdened by huge copper trading losses, said on Thursday it proposed to its labour union that summer bonuses of all employees be cut in an attempt to "pull up its socks".

"We caused our shareholders and our customers a lot of grief (through the copper losses). We have proposed cutting the bonuses of all employees in order to pull up the company's socks," a spokesman for Sumitomo said.
"The sharing of a bonus cut by all employees will mean making a fresh start to turn around the company," the spokesman said.
He added that the firm had already decided to cut the summer bonuses of top and middle-level executives in all departments.
He declined to say how much money would be saved by the bonus cuts.
Sumitomo announced last year that it lost $2.6 billion due to a decade of unauthorised copper trading by its former star trader Yasuo Hamanaka, who was fired in June 1996.
Sumitomo has denied any wrongdoing by the company, saying that the massive deals were made independently by Hamanaka and one of his former bosses without the knowledge of his superiors.

The giant trading house announced on Tuesday that it posted losses in the last business year for the first time since it was founded in 1919. It posted a parent net loss in the year to March 31 of 148.63 billion yen ($1.31 billion), compared with the previous year's net profit of 16.28 billion yen ($144 million).
The Sumitomo labour union was not immediately available for comment on the proposed bonus cuts.
